ACUTE ISCHAEMIC STROKE 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
<3 HOURS 
(CONSIDER IF WITHIN 3 - 4.5HOURS) 
 
*
TIME IS KEY - this must be done ASAP 
*
Urgent NON-CONTRAST CTB  
*
12 lead ECG 
*
Blood gas 
*
Lab: INR if indicated 
*
Perform NIHSS score 
*
Consider reperfusion therapy through shared 
decision-making 
*
Doctor to accompany patient to CT scan. 
Once radiologist confirms no intracranial 
haemorrhage/obvious infarct or any other 
pathology, the bolus dose of thrombolytic to be 
given in CT in consultation with ED consultant on 
call and written signed consent by patient or 
immediate family member. 
*
Thrombolytic infusion to be commenced in resus 
in the emergency department 
ACUTE STROKE ASSESSMENT 
* Time since onset of symptoms 
* Wake up stroke is currently not for thrombolysis 
* Consider/Exclude stroke mimics (see box) 
* Resuscitate (ABC approach) if patient is unstable 
* Keep Sat > 94% 
* Check HGT 
* Assess for swallowing  
* Use Stroke Jump bag in RESUS 
* Follow Stroke pathway below 
>4.5 HOURS 
 
*
Order urgent non-contrast CTB 
*
Consider contrast if alternative diagnosis is 
suspected 
*
12 lead ECG 
*
Blood gas  
*
Lab: FBC, U&E, INR if indicated 
*
Neurology referral 
EXCLUDE STROKE MIMICS 
*Hypoglycaemia 
*Seizures 
*Migraines 
*Tumours 
*Infection (abscess, meningitis) 
WHAT TO SAY TO PATIENT AND THEIR FAMILY 
                     REGARDING THROMBOLYSIS? 
 
*You are currently struggling from a stroke which means there is a  
   blood clot that is blocking blood flow in your brain. 
*There is currently a drug that can dissolve the clot, however it is  
   not perfect and has side-effects 
*The drug may improve some of the symptoms if given early but it  
  may not necessarily work and there is a chance that you can bleed  
  from the drug  
*1 in 6-10 patients may have improvement  
*1 in 20 may develop a significant bleed which can be life-threatening (5%) 
*If given between 3-4.5hrs risk of bleed increases to 8% 
GENERAL ED MANAGEMENT 
 
*Refer to the Critical Care Management    
  Principles Protocol for 
 
à Neuroprotective measures 
 
àFASTHUGS IN BED 
*Keep patients NPO  
*Nurse in left lateral position à high risk of  
  aspiration 
Contents

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
                    
THROMBOLYSIS EXCLUSION CRITERIA 
 
ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATIONS 
- Uncertain time of onset (last seen well >4.5hrs) 
- CT reveals an acute intracranial haemorrhage.  
- Recent severe head trauma (within 3 months)   
- History of intracranial/spinal surgery (within prior 3 months)  
- GI bleeding within past 21 days 
- INR >1.7 
- Mild non-disabling stroke (NIHSS <6) 
- Any improving neurology 
 
RELATIVE CONTRA-INDICATIONS 
- Hypo (<3.5mmol) or Hyper (>22.2mmol) glycaemia-correct prior to   
  thrombolysis 
- Pregnancy - to discuss with neurologist 
- Hypertension (systolic > 185mmHg /diastolic >110mmHg) 
  à to optimise before thrombolysis 
- Surgery or trauma with internal injuries (< 30
